severity: observation -- explains an outlier, changes no conclusion
what: A blended render of sac_s2@414000 on frozen condition 3 shows the robot KNOCKING the piston off the table rather than grasping it: horizontal displacement 0.1895 m and a lift of 0.1310 m with the grasp stage never firing.

chunk_12.note: lands BELOW its 0.889 start height -- off the support

chunk_13_to_22.note: stationary on the floor for the rest of the episode

is_it_the_blend.verdict: NO -- attributable to the known post-grasp nondeterminism.
is_it_the_blend.evidence: Three independent measurements of the SAME checkpoint and condition: stored n=50 (blend 0) gave reach only, disp 0.0106; a render (blend 0) gave reach+grasp, disp 0.0039; the blended render gave reach only, disp 0.1895. The two BLEND=0 runs already disagree with each other on whether grasp fires, so the divergence cannot be attributed to blending.
is_it_the_blend.caveat: This is n=1 per arm. A causal claim either way would need repeats, and the A/B that did use matched arms found no effect (carry 0.20 -> 0.16, inside noise).

notable: Condition 3 is one of the rare cases where even the GRASP stage diverges between identical runs. Grasp is 199/200 reproducible overall, so this is the ~0.5% tail rather than a counterexample to that claim.
why_it_matters: A knock-off produces a LARGE horizontal displacement (0.19 m) with no grasp. The frozen carry test requires lift, so it is correctly not scored as a carry -- but it is a reminder that displacement alone is not evidence of manipulation, and that any future metric keying on displacement without a grasp precondition would be exploitable.
